messages:
Harper: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands pricing/usage bit. Couple questions that came up on my team: 1) do we plan a smoothing/grace window to avoid immediate 429s during short traffic spikes (esp. during deploys)? 2) how do per-route quotas interact with org-level credits — is it possible to reserve credits for a high-priority route? 3) will rate-limit headers be standardized so client SDKs can backoff properly?

Leah (CEO): Great questions. Short answers: yes to smoothing (configurable window), yes to reserving for high-priority routes (enterprise feature), and yes to standard rate-limit headers. More detail below.

Riley (Platform): Smoothing design = leaky-bucket + transient buffer. Default smoothing window is 60s with a small burst allowance. Customers will be able to configure route-level smoothing and set a "priority_reserve" for critical routes on Enterprise plans. Example runtime policy: 

```
quota_smoothing:
  mode: leaky_bucket
  window_seconds: 60
  burst_tokens: 2x_avg
priority_reserve:
  route: "/v1/translate"
  reserved_tokens_per_min: 5000
```

Riley (Platform): For headers we're standardizing on: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, plus `X-Redwood-Quota-Window` when smoothing is active. We'll also include `Retry-After` on 429s. Example response header snippet: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1680000123
X-Redwood-Quota-Window: 60
Retry-After: 12
```

Jamal (SRE): Important: smoothing mustn't obscure noisy neighbors. Implementation note: smoothing is applied per-customer+route and we emit `smoothing_applied` metric with labels so infra can still trigger protective actions. Also we'll keep admission control at node level to maintain SLOs.

Sana (Finance): On credit reservation: enterprise contracts can purchase route reservations (we call them "priority pools"). Reserved credits reduce the org pool but are guaranteed for the route until consumed. Promo notes: we'll also support limited-time "sprint credits" for customers running hackweeks (apply via Sales). Billing note: reserved pools show as invoice line items for transparency.

Priya (Product): UX notes: Console will show a per-route card with current quota, smoothing status, reserved amount, and a small graph of estimated vs billed use. We'll add a toggle for smoothing and an "allocate reserve" flow for org admins (Enterprise-only during pilot).

Harper: That helps. One more: how will streaming partial responses be billed when smoothing is active or when a request is rate-limited mid-stream?

Riley (Platform): Streaming billing rule unchanged: tokens emitted are billed. If a stream gets cut by rate-limiting, we bill for tokens already emitted. We are exploring a refund heuristic for short-cancel windows (<200ms) but nothing committed. Smoothing only affects gating, not token accounting.

Jamal (SRE): Action: I'll add infra checks to ensure smoothing metrics are tagged and that smoothing doesn't change cache/KV eviction semantics. Also need tests that simulate bursty deploy traffic.

Sana (Finance): Action: I'll draft pricing language for "priority pools" and a sample invoice line. Also note that reserved pools affect overage thresholds and prepay top-up logic.

Priya (Product): Action: I'll create an RFC for quota smoothing + priority reserve UX and a pilot plan for a few enterprise customers. Will include header schema and acceptance criteria.

OpsBot: Draft internal explainer: https://redwood.internal/docs/pricing/quota-smoothing-and-priority-pools (bot).

Harper: Thanks all — I'll open a GH issue to track the RFC + infra validation. @Riley @Jamal @Sana @Priya please add ACs. :thumbsup:

Leah (CEO): Thanks team. We'll prioritize smoothing + headers in the infra roadmap for H2 and sync with Sales on pilot customers.
